subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation: autologous vs allogeneic, donor selection, conditioning regimens, graft-versus-host disease and infections

steps.tx: High-dose **Autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation** ASCT delivers supralethal myeloablative chemotherapy to eradicate chemosensitive malignancy, followed by re-infusion of the patient's own cryopreserved haematopoietic stem cells. ASCT serves as standard consolidation for fit patients with multiple myeloma and relapsed diffuse large B-cell or Hodgkin lymphoma, carrying negligible graft-versus-host disease risk and low treatment-related mortality.

left.title: Autologous Transplant (ASCT)
points: Source: Patient's own mobilised stem cells
Standard in myeloma and chemosensitive relapsed lymphoma

right.title: Allogeneic Transplant (Allo-HCT)
points: Source: Matched related, unrelated, or haploidentical donor
Carries substantial GVHD and graft failure risks
Standard in acute leukaemias and myelodysplastic syndrome

steps.tx: In contrast, **Allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation** allo-HCT replaces recipient haematopoiesis with healthy donor immune cells capable of exerting a potent, curative **graft-versus-leukaemia GVL** immunologic response. Donor alloreactive T-lymphocytes recognize minor histocompatibility antigens on recipient malignant clones, eradicating chemoresistant residual leukaemia stem cells and providing definitive long-term cure across high-risk acute leukaemias.

steps.tx: **Human leukocyte antigen** matching at 8 of 8 or 10 of 10 **high-resolution loci** HLA-A, B, C, DRB1, and DQB1 minimizes graft failure and graft-versus-host disease GVHD risk. Allelic mismatching at any locus significantly increases the incidence of primary graft rejection and transplant-related mortality.

steps.tx: The widespread adoption of **post-transplant cyclophosphamide** PTCy on days +3 and +4 has transformed **haploidentical stem cell transplantation**. Administering high-dose cyclophosphamide selectively destroys rapidly proliferating, highly alloreactive donor T cells that cause hyperacute GVHD, while sparing non-proliferating memory T cells and haematopoietic stem cells through high intracellular aldehyde dehydrogenase expression.

steps.tx: Acute **graft-versus-host disease** aGVHD classically manifests within the first 100 days following allogeneic transplantation, driven by donor T-cell mediated tissue damage. Diagnostic criteria evaluate three specific target organs: **skin maculopapular rash**, hepatic cholestasis with hyperbilirubinemia, and **gastrointestinal secretory diarrhoea**. First-line therapy for grade II to IV acute GVHD comprises high-dose systemic methylprednisolone.

steps.tx: **Ruxolitinib** oral JAK1 and JAK2 inhibitor significantly improves overall response rates and survival in acute and chronic **steroid-refractory GVHD** in the REACH2 and REACH3 trials. Inhibiting Janus kinase signalling suppresses downstream inflammatory cytokine transduction, producing rapid resolution of mucosal and cutaneous graft-versus-host manifestations.

points: Durable complete response rate significantly higher

right.title: REACH3 (Steroid-Refractory cGVHD)
points: Superior symptom reduction on Lee Symptom Scale

steps.tx: Hepatic **sinusoidal obstruction syndrome** SOS, formerly termed veno-occlusive disease VOD, is a life-threatening endothelial complication of myeloablative conditioning regimens containing busulfan or cyclophosphamide. Presenting with the classical triad of painful hepatomegaly, jaundice, and rapid ascites with fluid retention, severe cases carry high mortality and respond to the oligonucleotide **defibrotide**.

steps.tx: **Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome** usually appears within the first month after conditioning, with tender hepatomegaly, jaundice and fluid retention. The injury centres on hepatic sinusoidal endothelium. **Defibrotide** is the principal disease-directed treatment for severe disease. For **CMV** in seropositive allogeneic recipients, **antiviral prophylaxis** reduces clinically significant infection, and the choice of agent is guided by marrow toxicity and local protocol.

steps.tx: Reactivation of latent **Cytomegalovirus** CMV poses a formidable risk of life-threatening pneumonia and enteritis following allogeneic transplantation. Standard protocols mandate routine surveillance utilizing serial quantitative blood PCR. Early rising viral loads trigger preemptive therapy with intravenous **ganciclovir** or oral valganciclovir. Alternatively, letermovir CMV terminase complex prophylaxis provides effective primary prevention in seropositive recipients.
